analysis.summary: Bark and Qustodio are the only active publishers here. Bark pushes buyers toward its phone and watch, while Qustodio pushes research and parent guides. Life360 published nothing in 30 days.

points.text: Bark published 17 new pages and updated 29 in 30 days, so it is the most active rival, while Life360 had zero activity.
Bark refreshed many comparison pages against carriers and rival apps, including Qustodio, Gabb and Verizon. It wants parents who are ready to buy.
Qustodio mostly refreshed old research and guides (14 updates, 4 new pages). It is building trust with parents who are still learning.

shared.title: Parent guides on kids and social media
shared.text: Bark and Qustodio both publish guides on TikTok, teen mental health and online risks. Life360 has no recent pages to meet parents asking these questions.

shared.title: Phone-readiness advice
shared.text: Bark wrote about trick-or-treating alone and gradual phone access. Qustodio updated its 'Should I get my child a phone?' guide. Both reach parents before they pick a device.

gaps.title: Location sharing vs. monitoring
gaps.text: Neither active rival covers location sharing in the data. Life360 could own guides on when and how families should share location.

gaps.title: Driving safety for teens
gaps.text: No rival page in the data covers teen driving. Life360 could publish guides, data and checklists on new drivers.

gaps.title: Family apps comparison pages
gaps.text: Bark's comparisons focus on phones and parental control apps. None cover location-sharing apps, so Life360 could own that comparison.
